provenance: Agent-run sensitivity study using archived V3-derived geometry; no owner physical measurements or hardware tests.

policy.envelope: Centered conservative rectangular enclosure about the assumed axle midpoint; not a detailed mechanism or tire model.
policy.interval_bound: Nominal modeled interpolation only: min(endpoint clearances) - (translation + circumradius * absolute rotation radians)/2. Positive values give a conservative geometric separation bound using floating-point arithmetic, not a formally verified certificate.
policy.unresolved: Nonpositive interval bounds mean unresolved or colliding, not necessarily a detected collision. Inspect sampled hits separately.
policy.uncertainty: Inherited sampled constant-pose perturbations and one-at-a-time solid/target shifts. No simultaneous full-field errors, control dynamics or sensing.
policy.scope: Hypothetical fixed-route stress cases only. No avoidance planner, official obstacle legality, mission qualification, dimensional compliance or hardware selection.

assumptions: All added dimensions and obstacle poses are hypothetical engineering probes, not measurements or official legal obstacle configurations.
Envelope extents are measured from the assumed axle midpoint along body-forward, body-rear, body-left and body-right axes.
An asymmetric envelope is conservatively enclosed in a centered rectangle using twice the maximum opposing extent. Docking uses that rectangle too, not the actual mechanism outline.
Each envelope is held fixed for the entire route, including docking. No mechanism deployment sequence, tire geometry, height or envelope-rule compliance is established.
The routes are fixed. Blocked cases diagnose missing avoidance capability; this study does not plan a detour.
Between-sample clearance bounds apply only to nominal modeled paths. Uncertainty variants retain the inherited sampled checker.

End walls assumed present. Divider thickness is an assumed collision footprint, not the verified installed stock size.
Markings are excluded from collision solids for this conditional study; this is not an organizer ruling.
Obstacle polygons may be added as {id, vertices_in}; an empty list does not represent a competition-ready field.
Element shifts test one divider or target box at a time, not all simultaneous field variations. Board and stock dimensions remain fixed.
Position and heading errors are deterministic constant offsets along a route, not a localization or control model.
Waypoint interpolation permits sideways translation and in-place rotation. No differential-drive or steering constraints are enforced. Routes are independent maneuvers, not a connected legal mission.
Wheel track is a provisional calculation input, not a selected motor/wheel layout.
Axle midpoint is assumed to coincide with the center of the rectangular robot footprint.
Only straight forward/reverse and in-place spin primitives are used; no curved turns, slip, acceleration or actuator limits are modeled.
Each route connects assumed start pose, one illustrative divider circuit, assigned pit-box docking, reverse withdrawal, and return to race staging. It is not a complete legal competition mission.
Constant global position/heading perturbations in the inherited sweep are footprint-clearance stress tests, not integrated differential-drive odometry errors.
